title: Vendor demo: Tidepost helpdesk
scratchpad:
Tidepost demo - no decision
$65/agent/mo (escalation rules + help center plan)
macros import as-is -> tidy first
30 day sandbox, Lotte owns eval
segments: Thanks for having me. I'll keep the slides short and spend most of the time in the product, since you've all used a helpdesk before.
Please do. We're on Burrowdesk today, and we know exactly what we don't like about it, so show us the real thing.
The context is that our ticket volume has grown a lot this year, and the tool is slowing the team down more than the tickets are.
Understood. Let me start with macros, since that's usually what support teams care about first.
You can import macros straight from Burrowdesk. They come over exactly as they are, including the old ones nobody uses, so most teams tidy up before they move.
That's a polite way of saying our macros are a mess. We have a lot of duplicates with slightly different greetings.
Everyone does. Tidepost shows usage per macro from the first day, so the unused ones are easy to spot later on.
What about escalations? Today we escalate to engineering by hand, and things sit for days.
Escalation rules are timers. You define what urgent means, pick a timer, and when it runs out the ticket moves to an engineering queue and pings whoever you choose.
Can the timer differ by category? Login problems and invoice problems aren't the same kind of urgent at all.
Yes, per category, and per customer plan if you want. Most teams start with one rule and refine it once they've lived with it.
And reporting? I'd like to see first response time in business hours, not around the clock.
Business hours calendars are built in. Every report can be filtered to them, with weekends excluded if you like.
That alone would save me hours every month. Today I do it by hand in a spreadsheet.
Help center next. Articles have versions, and a screenshot can be swapped in every article that uses it, in one step.
That's the feature I'd pay for. Half our help articles still show screens from before the redesign.
Migration question. We have years of attachments in Burrowdesk. How does the import handle that?
Our importer is fast, but Burrowdesk's export interface is throttled, so big archives take a while on their side. Some teams only bring over the last two years and archive the rest.
Good to know before we plan anything.
Sixty five dollars per agent per month, on the plan with escalation rules and the help center.
That's more than we pay now, I think.
A bit more, yes. But we already pay in hours for everything Burrowdesk can't do.
I can set you up with a thirty day sandbox, with your real macros imported, so you can try it on actual work instead of my demo data.
Yes, let's do the sandbox. We'll decide after that. Nothing gets signed until the team has tried it on real tickets.
Agreed. Lotte owns the evaluation. Callum, can you help her pick the macros to test with?
Sure. I'll pick the ones we lean on most, so we see the import at its worst.
Great. I'll send the sandbox details this afternoon.

items.text: Tidepost costs $65 per agent per month on the plan with escalation rules and the help center
Run a thirty-day Tidepost sandbox before deciding; nothing signed until the team has tried it
